summary: Evening spike in 5xx during tenant warmup: connection shedding and runtime panic
description:
Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-12T19:05:00Z Acme Analytics (dedicated tenant) observed a sharp rise in 5xx responses from our API. The event coincided with a tenant warmup (scale-up) and a large embedding job. Error profiles: 502/503/504 with intermittent runtime OOM and NVML resets.

Initial impact: ~30-60% of requests returned 5xx over a 45-minute window. Streaming sessions experienced disconnects and retries, blocking customer traffic and triggering on-customer side retries.

Why this ticket: Customer reported production impact; they require a timeline, root cause hypothesis, and mitigation steps. SRE engaged for immediate containment.
impact: Acme Analytics production traffic: increased failed requests and latency; embeddings and text generation jobs partially failed. Uptime for their dedicated endpoint degraded below SLA for 45 minutes. Several downstream jobs timed out and retried, amplifying load.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer triggers tenant warmup by scaling target replica count from 2 -> 8 during business-hour traffic spike.
2) Simultaneously a scheduled bulk embedding upload (16k vectors) is processed by the tenant which issues many concurrent small requests.
3) API gateway experiences accept-queue pressure and begins shedding connections to lower priority routes.
4) Serving runtime nodes receive uneven fanout; some runtimes start reporting NVML resets and OOMs when prefetch and KV cache thrash.
5) Client sees high rate of 502/503/504 and long tail latencies; retries cause further amplification.
6) Errors reproduce under similar warmup + embedding mix in staging with limited load (non-prod cluster) when autoscaler threshold is lowered and connection backlog is high.
logs: 2026-03-12T19:06:12Z apigw[router] ERROR accept_queue_full route=tenant-acme weight=high backlog=4096
2026-03-12T19:06:17Z runtime[worker-5] ERROR nvml: GPU driver reset detected; pid=32211 model=gpt-redwood-1.3b
2026-03-12T19:07:18Z runtime[watchdog] ERROR process_exit pid=32211 signal=SIGABRT reason=OOM
2026-03-12T19:08:05Z apigw[router] WARN upstream_502 tenant=acme path=/v1/generate status=502 attempt=3
investigation_notes: 19:05 - Alerting: apigw SLO alert for increased 5xx rate for tenant-acme triggered (#alerts channel).
19:07 - Support engaged SRE and escalated to on-call. Customer-facing update posted and contact established (Acme SRE: Jordan Lee).
Hypothesis 1: Autoscaler warmup overshoot reduced overall per-node capacity due to noisy neighbor resource fragmentation during rapid scale-up.
Hypothesis 2: Accept-queue/backlog collapse in API gateway caused prioritizer to shed tenant connections; the shed traffic retried and amplified load on a subset of runtimes causing NVML resets.
Correlated signals: high KV cache eviction rates, prefetch lock timeouts, and NVML resets on 2/8 newly spun GPUs. No recent model patch was deployed to this tenant within the window.
Staging reproduction: Reproduced partial pattern by lowering autoscaler target and running synthetic concurrent embedding load; observed accept-queue saturation and a small number of runtime OOMs.
mitigation_actions: 19:12 - Put temporary per-tenant throttling (token rate) at API gateway for Acme to cap burst concurrency.
19:18 - Routed a portion of Acme traffic to a warmed fallback shard (separate node pool) to reduce fanout pressure.
19:25 - Disabled aggressive prefetch for the affected tenant to reduce KV cache churn.
19:40 - Removed autoscaler warmup override and reverted to conservative scale policy; started draining and reprovisioning two suspect runtimes.
20:05 - Full restart of 2 affected runtime pods after node replacement; NVML resets ceased and 5xx rate returned to baseline.
Customer communications: multiple updates (19:15, 19:35, 20:10) with ETA for full recovery and follow-up RCA commitment.
resolution_summary: Containment achieved by applying rate caps, routing traffic to warmed fallback nodes, disabling prefetch, and rolling out node replacements for unstable runtimes. Post-mitigation the 5xx rate dropped to baseline within ~25 minutes after restarts. A follow-up RCA is scheduled to confirm root cause and harden autoscaler and accept-queue behavior.
comments: Maya Patel (Support) [2026-03-12T19:14Z]: Initial acknowledgement to customer; escalating to SRE on-call. Asking for correlation IDs and traffic traces.
Jonas Klein (SRE) [2026-03-12T19:18Z]: Observed NVML resets on 2 runtime pods and high accept-queue backlog at apigw. Applying temporary rate cap and disabling prefetch for tenant-acme.
Jordan Lee (Acme SRE) [2026-03-12T19:20Z]: Confirmed heavy embedding batch started at 19:04Z. We're pausing the ingestion job while you remediate.
Jonas Klein (SRE) [2026-03-12T19:40Z]: Evicting suspect pods and rolling to new nodes; monitoring for NVML resets. Also reverting autoscaler warmup override as a precaution.
Maya Patel (Support) [2026-03-12T20:12Z]: Customer reports traffic returning to normal and embedding job resumed with reduced concurrency. Scheduling RCA and follow-ups with Eng and Product.

Jonas Klein (SRE) [2026-03-13T09:02Z]: Added telemetry hooks to accept-queue metrics and increased alert sensitivity for NVML resets during warmup. Follow-up action: patch autoscaler safety and ship backoff instrumentation (PRs linked).
